title: Snapshot
body:
## The Numbers That Reframe Everything

Dell Technologies entered fiscal year 2027 carrying a figure that reordered how investors understood the company: a $43 billion AI server backlog, representing roughly double the $24.6 billion in AI server revenue it had recognised across all of FY2026. That $24.6 billion — a growth rate exceeding 300 per cent year-on-year — is the single largest annual AI server revenue stream in the US enterprise hardware peer set outside the hyperscalers themselves. During FY2026, Dell closed more than $64 billion in AI server orders and shipped more than $25 billion. At a company reporting $113.5 billion in total revenue, roughly one dollar in five now traces directly to AI infrastructure.

Dell Technologies trades on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker **DELL**. Its principal offices are in Round Rock, Texas, where Michael S. Dell — founder, Chairman, and Chief Executive Officer for four continuous decades, interrupted only briefly when Kevin Rollins held the CEO title between 2004 and 2007 — continues to run the company he incorporated as PCs Limited in May 1984 from a University of Texas dormitory at age nineteen. Jeff Clarke serves as Vice Chairman and Chief Operating Officer, roles he has held since December 2019; Clarke oversees both reportable segments plus the global supply chain, making him the most operationally empowered non-Dell executive in the organisation. David Kennedy assumed the role of interim Chief Financial Officer on 11 September 2025, following Yvonne McGill's transition after nearly thirty years at Dell; the company has launched a comprehensive search for a permanent successor.

## Two Businesses, One Story

Dell operates through two reportable segments. Infrastructure Solutions Group — ISG — sells AI-optimised and traditional servers, storage, networking, and the Dell AI Factory platform; it is the segment where the current investment thesis lives. Client Solutions Group — CSG — sells commercial and consumer personal computers, including the emerging AI PC category incorporating Neural Processing Units, and provides the cash-generative base that funds working-capital intensity as ISG scales.

The FY2026 quarterly print illustrated how thoroughly the operating centre of gravity had shifted. In the fourth quarter, ISG generated [$18.82 billion in revenue](https://futurumgroup.com/insights/dell-q4-fy-2026-earnings-highlight-ai-optimized-server-ramp/), up 66 per cent year-on-year; within ISG, server and networking revenue grew 112 per cent. CSG contributed $13.5 billion for the quarter, up 14 per cent, with commercial the stronger sub-segment at $11.6 billion (+16 per cent) and consumer essentially flat at $1.9 billion. The AI PC refresh cycle was visible in commercial; the discretionary consumer market remained subdued.

|---|---|---|
| ISG Total | 18.82 | +66% |

| **FY2026 AI Server Revenue** | **24.6** | **+300%+** |

## Governance for a Cycle

The eight-person board pairs Michael Dell as Chairman with a group of independents weighted heavily toward operational CEO experience rather than financial engineering. Ellen Kullman, Lead Independent Director and Executive Chair of Carbon Inc., served as Chair and Chief Executive of DuPont through its 2008-to-2015 restructuring. Egon Durban, Co-Chief Executive of Silver Lake Management, has held a board seat since October 2013 — the moment of the original $24.4 billion take-private — giving him continuous visibility through the EMC acquisition, the 2018 NYSE relisting, the 2021 VMware spin, and now the AI server ramp. William Green, former Chairman and Chief Executive of Accenture, chairs the Audit Committee. Steven Mollenkopf, who ran Qualcomm from 2014 to 2021, provides direct semiconductor-CEO pattern recognition on chip supply and hyperscaler customer dynamics. David Dorman, Founding Partner of Centerview Capital Technology and former Chairman and Chief Executive of AT&T, brings telecommunications and technology-investing depth. David Grain, founder of infrastructure-focused private equity firm Grain Management, and Lynn Vojvodich Radakovich complete the roster.

The board has unanimously recommended Dell's redomestication from Delaware to Texas, aligning corporate domicile with operating reality in Round Rock — a move consistent with a broader trend among large US companies through 2025 and 2026.

## The Question the Dossier Answers

The $43 billion backlog is the asset; the question is conversion quality. Hyperscalers — whose procurement volumes define the top of the AI server market — retain the option to route future orders directly to original-design manufacturers: Inventec, Quanta, Wiwynn. Supermicro competes on price and speed-to-market in the GPU-dense configurations that dominate new AI cluster builds. Hewlett Packard Enterprise is pressing its ProLiant and Cray portfolio into the same enterprise accounts. Whether Dell's direct-sales force, supply-chain integration with NVIDIA, and Dell AI Factory software layer translate into AI server gross margins that hold at scale — or whether volume growth masks compression — is the central analytical question for any investor taking a position. This report assembles the evidence.
